name: Vocal cord filler injection
lead: Vocal cord filler injection, medically called injection laryngoplasty or injection augmentation, places material into a vocal fold to add bulk and move it toward the midline so the folds meet better. It is used clinically for vocal fold paralysis and weakness, and appearance-focused communities discuss it as a way to restore a fuller voice.[1]

Materials listed include autologous fat, collagen, hyaluronates, hydroxyapatite and others; effects of temporary materials last roughly 2 to 12 months.[1] Registered trials have examined silk-protein filler, platelet-rich fibrin with fat, and injection for voice tremor, all in patients with medical voice conditions.[2][3][4]

paras: Wikipedia reports that observation comes first, and if paralysis has not resolved after about 9 months and voice therapy is unsatisfactory, injection medialization is the next option.[1] Neither technique nor materials are standardised across clinicians.[1]

Trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov include a completed 11-patient study of silk protein microparticle filler for vocal cord paralysis and dysphonia (started 2020),[2] a 19-patient phase 4 study adding platelet-rich fibrin to autologous fat for vocal cord paralysis (started 2018),[3] and an 8-patient study of botulinum toxin and injection augmentation for essential voice tremor (started 2015).[4] Results are not summarised in the registrations. No studies were found of the procedure for cosmetic voice change in people without a voice disorder.
The procedure is mentioned in discussion of voice improvement among surgical options. The sources reviewed contain no community material to attribute.

card.summary: A clinical procedure that bulks a weak vocal fold; evidence is for medical voice disorders, not cosmetic use.
card.note: Medical procedure by a laryngologist; no cosmetic-use studies.

quick.overview:
Vocal fold injection puts filler into a weak or paralysed vocal fold so the folds close better, improving voice strength. Appearance communities mention it as a way to restore volume.

Studies are in patients with paralysis or tremor, not healthy people seeking cosmetic change.
quick.mechanism: Material such as fat, collagen or hyaluronate adds bulk and moves the fold toward the midline so it can vibrate against the other fold.
quick.risks: Temporary materials wear off in months, and techniques are not standardised. Specific complications are not detailed in the sources reviewed.
